content:
Cook visited Apple's Battersea campus in London this week and met with King Charles as part of a new partnership between Apple and the King's charitable trust fund.

At Apple's Battersea headquarters, Cook also gave an in-depth interview with The Independent, discussing the partnership and his feelings during his first month as Apple's Executive Chairman.

Cook stepped down as Apple's CEO last month, with John Ternus taking over. In this week's interview, he said the transition had 'actually started several years ago'.

Ternus takes over as CEO as the iPhone Duo launches, and Cook noted that the product's planning was already fully complete. He explained: 'I wanted to give John a tailwind, and at Apple, a tailwind basically comes from the product cycle.'

Cook also emphasised that as Executive Chairman, he focuses on 'global policy' matters and noted that there is 'an extremely high level of trust' between him and Ternus. Cook will assist Ternus in whatever way he deems appropriate, but stressed that he 'will not interfere.'

What advice did Cook give Ternus? 'Don't try to be another me.' The full interview is available at The Independent, which also details the new partnership between Apple and the King's charitable trust fund.
